sfda.why: The national register is authoritative for what is actually marketed in Saudi Arabia and for product-level facts no foreign source can supply: which brands exist here, which are suspended, and what each product contains beyond its active ingredient. Requested from the Authority on 2026-09-16.

sourcePolicy.model: Two independent references, each field carrying the one it came from. Neither replaces the other, and the split follows what each reference actually contains rather than where it comes from.
sourcePolicy.crossCheck: Holding both references is stronger than either alone: the wording is checked against an American plain-language source and a Saudi regulatory one, and the two must agree before a phrase is signed off.

medlineplus.why: Written from the outset for an ordinary reader at a defined reading level. Covers English and Spanish only; see sourcePolicy.languageReality. Every entry names the monograph URL, the section relied on and the date it was opened.

doesNotCover.sfdaLeaflets: The approved patient leaflets in the Tameni application do NOT carry dose or directions. Checked directly on 2026-09-16: the dosing section of a leaflet reads that the doctor will decide how much and when, with no figure given. This is structural, not an omission — a leaflet describes the product while a label directs the patient, and they are two documents with two purposes. Dose and directions therefore cannot come from the leaflets, and any claim that the catalogue rests on SFDA data alone would not survive the question of where the dose came from.
doesNotCover.sfdaLanguages: Arabic and English only. Urdu, Bengali, Indonesian and Spanish gain nothing from this source.

sourcePolicy.verification: SFDA leaflets are used as a VERIFICATION REFERENCE for the Arabic text: the reviewing pharmacist checks the project wording against the approved leaflet to confirm it neither contradicts it nor omits a material warning. The leaflets are not edited, abridged, quoted or reproduced. Abridging an approved leaflet was considered and rejected: deciding which of twenty listed adverse effects to drop is a clinical editorial act, the result would still carry the Authority's seal while the deletions were the researcher's, and the leaflet belongs to the marketing authorisation holder rather than to the Authority.
sourcePolicy.languageReality: CORRECTION, verified 2026-09-17. An earlier note in this policy said MedlinePlus carries the four draft languages. That was wrong and is retracted. The MedlinePlus drug monographs are AHFS Consumer Medication Information and exist in ENGLISH and SPANISH ONLY. The MedlinePlus collection advertised in more than fifty languages is a separate set of links to general health-topic material, not drug monographs, and it does not cover the medicines in this catalogue. The true position per language: English from MedlinePlus; Spanish from MedlinePlus; Arabic best taken from the SFDA approved leaflets, since an official Arabic text is stronger than a translation; and Urdu, Bengali and Indonesian have NO published reference of any kind. Those three are authored within the project and rest entirely on the native-speaker sign-off required by section 12.3 of the protocol, which has not yet been obtained. No data request to any authority or company changes this: the Saudi register is Arabic and English, MedlinePlus is English and Spanish, and neither holds the other three. This is the single largest open risk in the project and should be stated plainly wherever the language coverage is described.

ar.note:
CORRECTED 2026-09-19: sfda.gov.sa/en/drugs-list, recorded earlier, is the registered-products list; its detail pages carry no leaflet. The PIL and SPC are published on SDI, the Saudi Drug Information system (public pages sdi.sfda.gov.sa/home/Result?drugId=N). SDI and Tameni do not respond outside Saudi Arabia, so per-medicine drugIds must be recorded from inside the Kingdom.

2026-10-05: SFDA terms of use require written approval before linking to or copying content. A formal request was drafted (approval to deep-link SDI drug pages, and a PIL link or SDI drugId field in the Registered Drug API). Until approved the patient page opens the SDI portal.

bn.note:
Second search 2026-09-19, in depth. No medicines authority anywhere publishes a per-medicine leaflet in Bengali. Checked: DGDA (registration and price data; Bangladesh National Formulary is English; Drugs and Cosmetics Act 2023 sets no leaflet language, s.29 requires only a public list of registered drugs); MedlinePlus Bengali (vaccine statements only); manufacturers e.g. Square Pharmaceuticals (English prescribing PDFs only); NHS trusts serving Bengali communities (no translated medicine leaflets found). Bengali per-medicine text exists only on private indexes (MedEx by Ology Limited, DIMS Bangla app by Global Digital Apps) that cite no source and are written for professionals, and on Indian private-hospital sites. None is a regulator.

2026-10-05: no change — no authority publishes a per-medicine Bengali leaflet. A machine translation of the medicine's own MedlinePlus page (Google, translate.goog) is BUILT into the patient page but OFF (LEAFLET.machine.on = []), for the same reasons as Urdu.
bn.plan: Solution adopted 2026-09-20 (ph6.6), in place of a leaflet link that does not exist: (1) a validation pack — all 219 patient-facing strings exported with the English source, for back-translation by a native speaker who did not write them, reconciliation, and signature; the 17 phrases where a wrong word changes the dose or hides a danger are marked CRITICAL and signed first; every string was hash-checked against this database before export, and one Bengali string found altered in transit was restored. (2) a teach-back check with five patients per language at the counter (how much, when, how many days) — a signed phrase that three of five cannot repeat back is reworded. (3) a Listen button on the patient page that reads the medicine name, the directions and the missed-dose line aloud, shown ONLY when the phone actually holds a voice for that language, because a button that stays silent or speaks Urdu in an English voice costs more trust than it gains. (4) the pharmacist's spoken counselling remains the primary channel for these two languages. Until (1) and (2) are done, both languages stay unsigned drafts.
bn.decision: 2026-09-20, project owner: Bengali-speaking patients seen at the pharmacy mostly read neither Arabic nor English, so an Arabic or English leaflet link is NOT offered to them. Bengali content comes only from the reviewed dictionary, and native-speaker sign-off of that text is therefore the safety-critical step for this language.
bn.primarySources: Re-checked 2026-09-20. info.dgda.gov.bd/allopathic-medicines is DGDA's registered-medicine directory (brand, generic, strength, manufacturer, price) and could not even be opened by our reader because the portal's TLS certificate has expired; no per-medicine Bengali patient leaflet was found on it. Bengali per-medicine text still exists only on private indexes — MedEx (© Medex, a company, citing no regulator) and the DIMS Bangla app — which is the same finding as 19 Sep, now confirmed a second time. Conclusion unchanged: no authority publishes a linkable Bengali leaflet per medicine.

de.note: Germany's BfArM does not publish patient leaflets. Austria's BASG publishes the Gebrauchsinformation of every authorised medicine (medikamente.basg.gv.at/documents/<id>__DOTC_GEBR_INFO.pdf) in German. 27 of 28 were OPENED LIVE on 2026-09-20 and the product, ingredient and route confirmed, including the salt form and, for combinations, that no extra active ingredient is present. The 28th is apixaban, which links to the EMA product information in German (package leaflet is Annex IIIB); the document was confirmed as the Eliquis German PI but the reader could not reach the annex, so it stays title-confirmed. 4 combinations with no Austrian product open the register. GI 4.0 (Germany) is industry-run and not used.

id.note: REPLACED 2026-10-05. BPOM's PIONAS failed three times (incomplete certificate chain 2026-09-19, HTTP 503 2026-09-20, unreachable 2026-10-05) and its monographs are written for professionals. Malaysia's NPRA requires a consumer leaflet (RiMUP) for registered products and publishes it, in Bahasa Melayu and English, as an attachment on the product's QUEST3+ record. Bahasa Melayu and Bahasa Indonesia are standard forms of one language, so the patient page labels the document as Malay. Per medicine: one product whose only active ingredient(s) match, route matched from the product name, and whose attachment is explicitly the Malay version; the PDF was opened (HTTP 200) from Saudi Arabia on 2026-10-05.

ja.note: Per medicine: the PMDA patient guide PDF (info.pmda.go.jp/downfiles/...), or, where no guide exists, PMDA's own general-public drug page (pmda.go.jp/PmdaSearch/rdDetail/...?user=2). The general-public page for amoxicillin was OPENED LIVE on 2026-09-20 and confirmed as written for the public; the guide PDFs are disallowed to automated readers by PMDA's robots.txt, which we respect, so they stay title-confirmed. 19 linked, 13 open the guide index. Two closest matches are flagged in leafletMeta: diclofenac (Japan's tablet is the sodium salt) and ibuprofen (granules page).

ru.note: REPLACED 2026-10-05. tr.note: Per medicine: the approved Kullanma TalimatI PDF hosted by TITCK under titck.gov.tr/storage/kubKtAttachments/. 25 matched by product title, of which 7 were OPENED LIVE on 2026-09-20 and confirmed (Largopen, Lipitor, Concor, Zyrtec, Ciflosin, Oksapar, Ventolin); the remaining 18 could not be opened because the TITCK server repeatedly failed to serve robots.txt (HTTP 500) to our reader, so they stay title-confirmed and must be opened once before the language goes live. 7 medicines open the KUB/KT search page. One wrong match was caught and removed during checking: SEFAL is cinnarizine, not cefalexin. Prednol was deliberately not used for prednisolone because it is methylprednisolone.

ur.note:
Second search 2026-09-19, in depth. No medicines authority anywhere publishes a per-medicine leaflet in Urdu. Checked: DRAP (PIL guideline PE&R/GL/PL/005 sets no language and no online publication; price list and product index only; Pharmacy Services publishes English guidelines only); MedlinePlus Urdu (vaccine statements only); UK NHS / Health Innovation Network (general medicines-review leaflets, not per medicine); Hong Kong CHP (antibiotic-awareness posters only); Hong Kong HA drug leaflets (Chinese and English only). Nearest non-authority sources: AboutKidsHealth, SickKids Toronto (Urdu drug sheets for some medicines incl. paracetamol, amoxicillin, ciprofloxacin, ibuprofen, omeprazole, cefalexin; written for parents of children; some dated 2008); Aga Khan University Hospital Karachi (Urdu insulin brochure; other medicine leaflets are image PDFs, language not confirmed); Arthritis Australia (paracetamol, NSAIDs). None is a regulator.

2026-10-05: re-checked DRAP (SmPC page, PIL guideline) — still no per-medicine Urdu leaflet online. A machine translation of the medicine's own MedlinePlus page (Google, translate.goog) is BUILT into the patient page but OFF (LEAFLET.machine.on = []). It breaks this register's rule that the patient reads an original, and an unreviewed translation can carry a wrong warning; switching it on is a decision for the supervisor and the ethics committee.
ur.plan: Solution adopted 2026-09-20 (ph6.6), in place of a leaflet link that does not exist: (1) a validation pack — all 219 patient-facing strings exported with the English source, for back-translation by a native speaker who did not write them, reconciliation, and signature; the 17 phrases where a wrong word changes the dose or hides a danger are marked CRITICAL and signed first; every string was hash-checked against this database before export, and one Bengali string found altered in transit was restored. (2) a teach-back check with five patients per language at the counter (how much, when, how many days) — a signed phrase that three of five cannot repeat back is reworded. (3) a Listen button on the patient page that reads the medicine name, the directions and the missed-dose line aloud, shown ONLY when the phone actually holds a voice for that language, because a button that stays silent or speaks Urdu in an English voice costs more trust than it gains. (4) the pharmacist's spoken counselling remains the primary channel for these two languages. Until (1) and (2) are done, both languages stay unsigned drafts.
ur.decision: 2026-09-20, project owner: Urdu-speaking patients seen at the pharmacy mostly read neither Arabic nor English, so an Arabic or English leaflet link is NOT offered to them. Urdu content comes only from the reviewed dictionary, and native-speaker sign-off of that text is therefore the safety-critical step for this language.
ur.primarySources: Checked against DRAP's own documents on 2026-09-20, not against summaries. (1) PATIENT INFORMATION LEAFLET (PIL) GUIDELINES, document PE&R/GL/PL/005: contains no clause requiring Urdu, and no obligation on DRAP to publish leaflets online or keep a public database of them; the leaflet is held by the marketing authorisation holder and travels inside the pack. (2) GUIDELINES ON LABELING AND PACKING OF PHARMACEUTICAL AND BIOLOGICAL DRUGS v1.0 (2024), section 6.1(h): Urdu IS required, but only for three things, printed on the pack — the name of the drug, the dosage, and the instructions. (3) eapp.dra.gov.pk/WebProductIndex.php is a registration search (registration number, brand, generic); no leaflet is attached. Conclusion unchanged and now evidenced from primary sources: Urdu patient text exists in Pakistan on the pack, and nowhere online that can be linked per medicine. Worth carrying into the ethics file: what DRAP mandates in Urdu — name, dose, instructions — is exactly the scope this project prints on the label.

zh.note: UPDATED 2026-10-05. The CAPTCHA seen on 2026-09-20 sits on the SEARCH page only. The licence page of a product (mcp.fda.gov.tw/im_detail_1/<licence no.>) opens directly, without a CAPTCHA, and carries the whole insert in sections, including section 14, information for the patient. Per medicine: one product with a valid licence and an insert on file, chosen from TFDA open data (data.fda.gov.tw datasets 37 and 39), single ingredient (or the exact combination), route matched from the dosage form. TFDA's robots.txt disallows automated readers on mcp.fda.gov.tw, which we respect: the licence page format was opened by hand, and each link is opened by the reviewer. The insert is closer to an SmPC than a lay leaflet.
zh.document: 仿單 (package insert; section 14 病人使用須知 = patient information)
zh.phoneTest: 2026-10-04: licence page opened in a browser on the owner's laptop in Saudi Arabia, no CAPTCHA. Open one link on a phone after deploying ph6.26.

leafletSources._key: The link is resolved by the International Nonproprietary Name, which is written in Latin script by every authority in the world and is therefore the one identifier that crosses all of them.
leafletSources._model: The patient page offers, alongside the pharmacist's own instructions, a link to the official medicines-authority leaflet in the patient's own language, published by the authority of the country where that language is official. Only the link is held; the text is never copied. The patient reads an original written in their language, not a translation.

_tiers.registryOnly: An official and trusted authority, but the listed portal is a registration, price or tracking register, not a leaflet. Recorded for brand and registration matching; never shown to the patient as 'the leaflet', because a patient who opens it finds no instructions.
_tiers.patientLeaflet: The portal serves the patient leaflet itself, in that language, to the public. Shown on the patient page.

_status.portal: No per-drug match; the link opens the authority's search page.
_status.verified: Portal opened and a leaflet seen.
_status.searched-none: Searched in depth, including other countries where the language is official; no official per-medicine source exists.
_status.verified-live: Per-drug document opened by us and the product, ingredient and route confirmed.
_status.none-in-country: No product with this ingredient is authorised in that country; no link is shown.
_status.title-confirmed: Per-drug document matched by its official title in the authority's own index; the document itself was not opened (often because the site disallows automated readers).
_status.search-confirmed: The leaflet document type is indexed at that portal; page not yet opened by us (2026-09-19). Open one leaflet before the language goes live.
_status.pattern-confirmed: Per-drug link is the authority's own search URL pre-filled with the INN; it lists products and the patient chooses one.
_status.verified-authority: The authority is official; the portal serves no leaflet.
_status.blocked-for-patient: The portal is official and it opens, but a patient cannot actually reach the document — a CAPTCHA stands in the way, or the server is unreliable. Recorded from a real test on a phone, not assumed. The language is not offered.

leafletSources._enabled: Linked languages (fr, tr, de, ja, ru, zh) were added 2026-09-20 in mode 'linked': the label prints only the dose slots (amount, frequency, timing, duration), the missed-dose advice and one line pointing to the official leaflet; purpose and warnings are NOT translated and are not printed for them, and everything else about the medicine comes from the linked official leaflet. All their strings are unsigned drafts (reviewed=false) until a native speaker signs them. fa has no source and is not added. ur and bn keep the full reviewed dictionary and are deliberately offered NO leaflet link (project-owner decision 2026-09-20). 2026-10-05 (site ph6.26): ru switched to RCETH Belarus patient leaflets (GRLS dropped: CAPTCHA), zh to TFDA licence pages (病人使用須知), id to NPRA Malaysia RiMUP in Bahasa Melayu (BPOM/PIONAS has no per-medicine patient leaflet). ar waits on SFDA written approval (portal until then). ur and bn: still no regulator source; a machine-translation option is built into the patient page but OFF pending supervisor and ethics approval.
leafletSources._governs: The printed label always governs. The linked leaflet may describe a product registered in another country, whose brand, strength or approved uses can differ. The patient page states this in the patient's own language above every link.
leafletSources._perDrug: drugs.<key>.leafletRefs holds one URL per language, keyed by INN. A string opens that document; null means no product with this ingredient is authorised in that country, so no link is shown; an empty string falls back to the portal. leafletMeta records which product was chosen and why.
leafletSources._directory: Imported 2026-09-19 from the two directories supplied by the project owner (12 countries), then each portal was opened or searched for what it actually serves to the public. Where the directory's portal serves no leaflet, an official alternative was sought in that country or in another country where the language is official.

outro.es: Le recordaremos hasta el final del tratamiento. Para detenerlo, toque aquí:
outro.fr: Nous vous le rappellerons jusqu'à la fin du traitement. Pour arrêter, touchez ici :
outro.hi: इलाज ख़त्म होने तक हम आपको याद दिलाते रहेंगे। बंद करने के लिए यहाँ टैप करें:
outro.id: Kami akan mengingatkan Anda hingga pengobatan selesai. Untuk berhenti, ketuk di sini:
outro.ja: 治療が終わるまでお知らせします。停止するにはここをタップ：
outro.ms: Kami akan mengingatkan anda sehingga rawatan tamat. Untuk berhenti, ketik di sini:
outro.ru: Мы будем напоминать до конца лечения. Чтобы отключить, нажмите здесь:
outro.tl: Ipapaalala namin sa iyo hanggang matapos ang gamutan. Para itigil, pindutin dito:
outro.tr: Tedavi bitene kadar size hatırlatacağız. Durdurmak için buraya dokunun:
outro.ur: علاج ختم ہونے تک ہم آپ کو یاد دلاتے رہیں گے۔ روکنے کے لیے یہاں دبائیں:
outro.zh: 我们会提醒您直到疗程结束。如需停止，请点此处：

lastDose.ar: — هذه آخر جرعة. العلاج يكتمل بعدها، ولن تصلك رسائل تذكير إضافية لهذا الدواء.
lastDose.bn: — এটি শেষ ডোজ। চিকিৎসা এখন সম্পূর্ণ; এই ওষুধের জন্য আর কোনো রিমাইন্ডার পাবেন না।
lastDose.de: — Dies ist die letzte Dosis. Die Behandlung ist abgeschlossen; Sie erhalten keine weiteren Erinnerungen für dieses Arzneimittel.
lastDose.en: — This is the last dose. Treatment is now complete; you won't receive further reminders for this medicine.
lastDose.es: — Esta es la última dosis. El tratamiento ya está completo; no recibirá más recordatorios para este medicamento.
lastDose.fr: — C'est la dernière dose. Le traitement est terminé ; vous ne recevrez plus de rappels pour ce médicament.
lastDose.hi: — यह आख़िरी ख़ुराक है। इलाज अब पूरा हो गया; इस दवा के लिए आपको और याद-संदेश नहीं मिलेंगे।
lastDose.id: — Ini adalah dosis terakhir. Pengobatan kini selesai; Anda tidak akan menerima pengingat lagi untuk obat ini.
lastDose.ja: — これが最後の1回です。治療は終わりました。この薬のお知らせはこれで終わりです。
lastDose.ms: — Ini dos yang terakhir. Rawatan anda kini selesai; anda tidak akan menerima peringatan lagi untuk ubat ini.
lastDose.ru: — Это последняя доза. Лечение завершено; напоминаний об этом лекарстве больше не будет.
lastDose.tl: — Ito na ang huling dosis. Tapos na ang gamutan; hindi ka na makatatanggap ng paalala para sa gamot na ito.
lastDose.tr: — Bu son dozdur. Tedavi tamamlandı; bu ilaç için başka hatırlatma almayacaksınız.
lastDose.ur: — یہ آخری خوراک ہے۔ علاج اب مکمل ہو چکا؛ اس دوا کے لیے مزید یاد دہانیاں موصول نہیں ہوں گی۔
lastDose.zh: ——这是最后一次用药。疗程已完成，本药不会再发送提醒。

subjectWelcome.hi: आपकी दवा दे दी गई है
subjectWelcome.ja: お薬をお渡ししました
